findings.title: deleteCache removes cache for any credential the user owns, not only Google Calendar, and ignores delegation credentials
findings.body: The handler only checks that the credential belongs to the user, then deletes all calendarCache rows for that credentialId. The UI exposes this only for Google Calendar, but the endpoint itself accepts any credential id. Delegation-credential calendars are looked up by userId rather than credentialId in the cache repository, so deleting by credentialId will not clear the cache entries that are actually used for them, and the success response will mislead the user.

findings.title: Cache status is queried on every connectedCalendars call, including for non-calendar and empty credential lists
findings.body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds is called unconditionally on every request to connectedCalendars, which is used across settings and onboarding pages. It runs a groupBy over CalendarCache for every call, even when there are no connected calendars. This adds a DB round trip to a hot read path just to populate a timestamp that is only displayed for Google Calendar.

findings.title: groupBy on credentialId with empty array filter returns unexpected results and is not scoped to valid rows
findings.body: When credentialIds is empty, Prisma's `in: []` yields no rows, which is fine, but the method also does not filter expired entries, so the 'last updated' timestamp shown reflects stale rows that were already expired or are being used for a different key. The status is per-credential max updatedAt across all keys, which does not represent whether the cache is currently valid.

findings.title: updatedAt added with @updatedAt on a table that is written via upsert on userId-only paths
findings.body: The new updatedAt column uses @default(now()) @updatedAt. Prisma's @updatedAt is set on every Prisma update, but the raw SQL migration uses DEFAULT NOW() with no matching trigger. Rows touched by raw SQL or by the legacy-userId update path will have inconsistent semantics, and the displayed 'last updated' value may not reflect when data was actually refreshed.

findings.title: updateManyByCredentialId on every cache refresh bumps SelectedCalendar.updatedAt for all calendars of the credential
findings.body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache now calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(credentialId, {}) after every cache write. This updates all selected calendar rows for the credential, including unrelated event-type scoped ones, on each refresh and webhook. It also has no effect on the UI as the PR notes, adding write load for no displayed value. The PR itself suggests it should be removed.

findings.title: Dropdown hides cache deletion and disconnect for non-Google, and renders empty trigger when cacheUpdatedAt is a falsy-but-valid value
findings.body: hasCache is `isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt`, which returns the Date object or null. The conditional rendering is then mixed with the early return on `!canDisconnect && !hasCache`, so for a delegated Google credential with no cache the component returns null, but for a delegated Google credential with cache it still shows the trigger yet hides 'Remove app' correctly. Behavior is correct but fragile; more importantly the early return happens after hooks, which is fine, so the real issue is the 'Remove app' menu item is hidden when delegation is set while the cache-delete item shows without any confirmation context for delegated calendars.

findings.title: Date formatting hard-coded to en-US and ignores user locale
findings.body: The timestamp uses Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US") rather than the user's locale from useLocale, so the displayed date is inconsistent with the rest of the translated UI. Additionally new Date(cacheUpdatedAt) is called on a value that may arrive serialized as a string over tRPC, so the type annotation Date | null is not what is actually received at runtime.

findings.title: deleteCache mutation onSuccess does not invalidate connectedCalendars, so cache status does not refresh
findings.body: The deleteCache mutation's success handler only shows a toast and calls onSuccess. It does not invalidate trpc.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars, so the cacheUpdatedAt shown in the dropdown stays stale until a manual refresh, contrary to the PR's expectation that the UI updates.

findings.title: deleteCache uses a raw z.number() input instead of a shared schema and does not check the credential type
findings.body: The new procedure defines its input inline rather than in a schema file like the other calendar procedures. It accepts any credential id and no integration type, so the server contract allows deleting cache for non-calendar credentials.

findings.title: sed -i '' is macOS-only and the script runs unconditionally against the repo .env
findings.body: `sed -i ''` fails on GNU/Linux, so the script breaks in Linux dev environments and CI. The script also rewrites ../.env in place without a backup, and the cleanup handler exits 0 even on the rate-limit failure path.

findings.title: Confirmation text says action cannot be undone but the cache is regenerated automatically
findings.body: The 'confirm_delete_cache' string warns that the action cannot be undone, which overstates the impact since the cache is rebuilt on the next availability request. Also 'cache_last_updated' is passed a preformatted timestamp, so the translation key's placeholder name is coupled to the formatting done in the component.
